resolution.title: Fix query builder to find translations by key in Backoffice during the translations saving process
resolution.description: This PR fixes some rare cases where the saving of some translations are impossible using the Backoffice interface. Specifically, whenever you had two or more similar (starting with the same text) translation keys within the same domain, where each one is using a % character (eg. '%s') in their key, this will create an unwanted behaviour where you will be able to traslate just one key, because the query will pull a result everytime since it's using LIKE with the special %s character. I'm proposing to change the LIKE operator to an equal sign, since we must find the exact match by translation key.
resolution.how_to_test: Create two similar translations keys within the same domain, either in a .tpl file or in a module (doesn't matter). Eg: "Hello %s, welcome back" and "Hello %s". Try to translate them.

When the cache is cleared, the system increments the `PS_CCCCSS_VERSION` and `PS_CCCJS_VERSION` configurations based on the selected shop context. However:

- If the operation is performed while selecting a **single shop**, the configurations are correctly updated only for that specific shop.
- If the cache is cleared while selecting "**All stores**", the system updates only the global configurations and not those of individual shops.

As a result, if the cache was previously cleared for a single shop and then cleared again globally, the individual shop’s configurations are not updated. This causes the front-office to use outdated assets, leading to display and loading issues.
ticket.steps:
1. Enable Multishop:
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Multistore and enable the multishop feature.
    - Create at least two shops.

2. Enable JS and CSS Caching:
    - Navigate to Advanced Parameters > Performance.
    - Under the CCC (Combine, Compress, and Cache) section, enable:
        -  Smart cache for JavaScript
        -  Smart cache for CSS
    - Save the settings.
3. Clear Cache for a Single Shop:
    -  In the multishop selector (top-left of the back office), select a single shop.
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Performance and click Clear cache.
    - This will update the "PS_CCCJS_VERSION" and "PS_CCCJS_VERSION" values for the selected shop.
4. Clear Cache for All Shops:
    - In the multishop selector, choose "All stores".
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Performance and click Clear cache again.
    - This updates only the global configurations but does not affect individual shop configurations.
5. Check the Issue in the Front-Office:
    - Visit the front-office of the previously selected single shop.
    - The shop continues to load outdated JavaScript and CSS assets instead of the refreshed ones.

resolution.title: Fix: Issue with JS and CSS cache clearing in multishop context
resolution.description: see https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/38135

ticket.title: [Bug] Missing attributes autoplay, loop, muted, and playsinline in the video tag within Tools::purifyHTML()
ticket.bug:

- src
- type
- width
- height
- poster
- preload
- controls

However, the following attributes are missing:
- autoplay
- loop
- muted
- playsinline

These attributes are essential for the proper functioning of HTML5 videos, especially for:
- Allowing autoplay (necessary for, for example, background videos);
- Enabling loop;
- Ensuring silent autoplay (as required by browsers);
- Enabling inline playback on mobile devices (avoiding the transition to fullscreen).

2. In  cms page insert anHTML block containing the following code:
 ```html
<video autoplay="autoplay" loop="loop" muted="muted" playsinline="playsinline">
    <source src="VIDEO_URL" type="video/mp4">
</video>
```
3. Save the content.
4. Observe that the resulting code is "cleaned", with the desired attributes removed:
 ```html
<video>
    <source src="VIDEO_URL" type="video/mp4">
</video>
```

Do you think it would make sense to enable these attributes? I could create a PR regarding this.

Thank you.

ticket.title: Currency conversion is run even if there is set a specific price for a currency
ticket.bug:
When a merchant has 2 or more currencies, one can set a currency conversion. Lets say NOK and EUR. 
NOK is default price and EUR is set to conversion 0,1, meaning a product priced to 100 NOK, should be converted to 10 EUR. This works fine. 

But when a merchant wants to set the price for EUR specifically, lets say he/she sets it to 8 EUR with a specific price, the automatic currency conversion **should not apply**, however it does. 

In this case the price 8 EUR would be converted to 0,8 EUR.
ticket.expected: When specific price is set for a currency, automatic currency conversion should not apply.
ticket.steps:
1. Create a product.
2. Activate two or more currencies, set up  currency conversion numbers.
3. Observe in front office that the price change as expected with automatic currency conversion.
4. Now go to the product and set a specific price for a currency.
5. Observe in front office that BOTH your "manual" specific price currency conversion AND the automatic currency conversion is applied.


Now, here is the sollution:
```
classes/Product.php:3896
$id_currency == $specific_price['id_currency'] // instead of strict check $id_currency === $specific_price['id_currency']
```

6. Now observe it works as it should.

The reason is that `$id_currency` is a string and `$specific_price['id_currency']`  is an int (or the other way, I cant remember), so the typesafe condition fails.

The bug should possibly be solved by making sure both those variables are int`s, but a quick fix is to disable the typecheck.

resolution.title: Fix Incorrect SpecificPrice Currency Conversion (Issue 36844)
resolution.description: Specific Prices have a currency conversion applied to them even if the currency has been set and no conversion is necessary. See issue for full details.
resolution.how_to_test: For a product set a "Specific Price" that does not use the default shop currency and view the item in the store in the same currency. If an exchange rate is set then the price should still match the one set in the back office and the exchange rate will not be applied.

ticket.title: Incompatibility Issue with PDO Returning Integer Values with PHP 8.1
ticket.bug:
When using PHP 8.1 with PrestaShop 8.0 (minimal version that support PHP 8.1), the function executeS() from the Db class returns integers for columns that are defined as tinyInt or unsignedInt in the database. In previous PHP versions (before 8.1), the values returned were always strings, regardless of the column type.

This change in behavior is due to PHP 8.1 no longer automatically casting values to strings. Unfortunately, many modules have historically relied on these values being returned as strings, which causes issues when comparing values like '1' === 1.

As a result, module integrations expecting stringified values are disrupted, leading to compatibility issues across PrestaShop versions that support PHP 8.1.

This breaking change is documented here : https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration81.incompatible.php#migration81.incompatible.pdo.sqlite

Exemple with Db->executeS() on ps_product table. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a232848-bedd-488d-a0a7-f4268b9e220d)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c97d0c1f-286f-40a4-bd96-6d68057fb8b1)
ticket.expected:
The "PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES" parameter should be set to true on the PDO instance to maintain the historical behavior and avoid breaking changes.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab8f0b3b-04a1-4532-b58c-efcf70b33296)

resolution.title: Add attr_stringify_fetches to PDO init config to avoid BC Break

ticket.title: Problems OrderProductForViewing "must be of type string (or int), null given" and Memcached
ticket.bug:
I had a problem with retrieving the stock location for products that are no longer available when viewing an old order. Normally, this should return false when the stock location is not found. But when the Memcached cache is active, the null value is returned, causing a fatal error. This must be linked to the fact that Memcached doesn't distinguish between null and false. 

To correct my specific problem, I added the following processing at the end of the setProductCurrentStock() method in /classes/order/Order.php:
```
if ($product['location'] === null) {
    $product['location'] = false;
}
```

This ensures that false is returned and not null. 

The following issues seem to be affected by a similar bug: 
[#22215](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/22215)
[#35753](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/35753)
[#35979](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/35979)

ticket.title: Issue with JS and CSS cache clearing in multishop context
ticket.bug:
In a multishop environment with at least two stores, when enabling JavaScript or CSS caching (_Advanced Parameters > Performance > CCC (Combine, Compress, and Cache) > Smart cache for JavaScript / Smart cache for CSS_), an issue occurs when clearing the cache.

When the cache is cleared, the system increments the `PS_CCCCSS_VERSION` and `PS_CCCJS_VERSION` configurations based on the selected shop context. However:

- If the operation is performed while selecting a **single shop**, the configurations are correctly updated only for that specific shop.
- If the cache is cleared while selecting "**All stores**", the system updates only the global configurations and not those of individual shops.

As a result, if the cache was previously cleared for a single shop and then cleared again globally, the individual shop’s configurations are not updated. This causes the front-office to use outdated assets, leading to display and loading issues.
ticket.steps:
1. Enable Multishop:
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Multistore and enable the multishop feature.
    - Create at least two shops.

2. Enable JS and CSS Caching:
    - Navigate to Advanced Parameters > Performance.
    - Under the CCC (Combine, Compress, and Cache) section, enable:
        -  Smart cache for JavaScript
        -  Smart cache for CSS
    - Save the settings.
3. Clear Cache for a Single Shop:
    -  In the multishop selector (top-left of the back office), select a single shop.
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Performance and click Clear cache.
    - This will update the "PS_CCCJS_VERSION" and "PS_CCCJS_VERSION" values for the selected shop.
4. Clear Cache for All Shops:
    - In the multishop selector, choose "All stores".
    - Go to Advanced Parameters > Performance and click Clear cache again.
    - This updates only the global configurations but does not affect individual shop configurations.
5. Check the Issue in the Front-Office:
    - Visit the front-office of the previously selected single shop.
    - The shop continues to load outdated JavaScript and CSS assets instead of the refreshed ones.

resolution.title: Fix: Issue with JS and CSS cache clearing in multishop context
resolution.description: see https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/issues/38135
resolution.author: Codencode

ticket.title: [Bug] Missing attributes autoplay, loop, muted, and playsinline in the video tag within Tools::purifyHTML()
ticket.bug:
Currently, the `Tools::purifyHTML()` function defines the <video> element with the following allowed attributes:
- src
- type
- width
- height
- poster
- preload
- controls

However, the following attributes are missing:
- autoplay
- loop
- muted
- playsinline

These attributes are essential for the proper functioning of HTML5 videos, especially for:
- Allowing autoplay (necessary for, for example, background videos);
- Enabling loop;
- Ensuring silent autoplay (as required by browsers);
- Enabling inline playback on mobile devices (avoiding the transition to fullscreen).
ticket.steps:
1. Enable the "Use HTMLPurifier Library" option in the PrestaShop back office.
2. In  cms page insert anHTML block containing the following code:
 ```html
<video autoplay="autoplay" loop="loop" muted="muted" playsinline="playsinline">
    <source src="VIDEO_URL" type="video/mp4">
</video>
```
3. Save the content.
4. Observe that the resulting code is "cleaned", with the desired attributes removed:
 ```html
<video>
    <source src="VIDEO_URL" type="video/mp4">
</video>
```

Do you think it would make sense to enable these attributes? I could create a PR regarding this.

Thank you.

resolution.title: Fix: [Bug] Missing attributes autoplay, loop, muted, and playsinline in the video tag within Tools::purifyHTML()

ticket.title: Currency conversion is run even if there is set a specific price for a currency
ticket.bug:
When a merchant has 2 or more currencies, one can set a currency conversion. Lets say NOK and EUR. 
NOK is default price and EUR is set to conversion 0,1, meaning a product priced to 100 NOK, should be converted to 10 EUR. This works fine. 

But when a merchant wants to set the price for EUR specifically, lets say he/she sets it to 8 EUR with a specific price, the automatic currency conversion **should not apply**, however it does. 

In this case the price 8 EUR would be converted to 0,8 EUR.
ticket.expected: When specific price is set for a currency, automatic currency conversion should not apply.
ticket.steps:
1. Create a product.
2. Activate two or more currencies, set up  currency conversion numbers.
3. Observe in front office that the price change as expected with automatic currency conversion.
4. Now go to the product and set a specific price for a currency.
5. Observe in front office that BOTH your "manual" specific price currency conversion AND the automatic currency conversion is applied.


Now, here is the sollution:
```
classes/Product.php:3896
$id_currency == $specific_price['id_currency'] // instead of strict check $id_currency === $specific_price['id_currency']
```

6. Now observe it works as it should.

The reason is that `$id_currency` is a string and `$specific_price['id_currency']`  is an int (or the other way, I cant remember), so the typesafe condition fails.

The bug should possibly be solved by making sure both those variables are int`s, but a quick fix is to disable the typecheck.

resolution.title: Fix Incorrect SpecificPrice Currency Conversion (Issue 36844)
resolution.description: Specific Prices have a currency conversion applied to them even if the currency has been set and no conversion is necessary. See issue for full details.
resolution.how_to_test: For a product set a "Specific Price" that does not use the default shop currency and view the item in the store in the same currency. If an exchange rate is set then the price should still match the one set in the back office and the exchange rate will not be applied.
resolution.author: mrkalchemy

ticket.title: Incompatibility Issue with PDO Returning Integer Values with PHP 8.1
ticket.bug:
When using PHP 8.1 with PrestaShop 8.0 (minimal version that support PHP 8.1), the function executeS() from the Db class returns integers for columns that are defined as tinyInt or unsignedInt in the database. In previous PHP versions (before 8.1), the values returned were always strings, regardless of the column type.

This change in behavior is due to PHP 8.1 no longer automatically casting values to strings. Unfortunately, many modules have historically relied on these values being returned as strings, which causes issues when comparing values like '1' === 1.

As a result, module integrations expecting stringified values are disrupted, leading to compatibility issues across PrestaShop versions that support PHP 8.1.

This breaking change is documented here : https://www.php.net/manual/en/migration81.incompatible.php#migration81.incompatible.pdo.sqlite

Exemple with Db->executeS() on ps_product table. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a232848-bedd-488d-a0a7-f4268b9e220d)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c97d0c1f-286f-40a4-bd96-6d68057fb8b1)
ticket.expected:
The "PDO::ATTR_STRINGIFY_FETCHES" parameter should be set to true on the PDO instance to maintain the historical behavior and avoid breaking changes.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab8f0b3b-04a1-4532-b58c-efcf70b33296)

resolution.title: Add attr_stringify_fetches to PDO init config to avoid BC Break
resolution.description: Fix Incompatibility Issue with PDO Returning Integer Values with PHP 8.1
resolution.how_to_test: dump a response from database returned by PDO, and check type of values.

ticket.title: Problems OrderProductForViewing "must be of type string (or int), null given" and Memcached
ticket.bug:
I had a problem with retrieving the stock location for products that are no longer available when viewing an old order. Normally, this should return false when the stock location is not found. But when the Memcached cache is active, the null value is returned, causing a fatal error. This must be linked to the fact that Memcached doesn't distinguish between null and false. 

To correct my specific problem, I added the following processing at the end of the setProductCurrentStock() method in /classes/order/Order.php:
```
if ($product['location'] === null) {
    $product['location'] = false;
}
```

This ensures that false is returned and not null. 

The following issues seem to be affected by a similar bug: 
[#22215](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/22215)
[#35753](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/35753)
[#35979](https://github.com/PrestaShop/PrestaShop/pull/35979)

3. Delete an ordered product from the catalog
4. View order
